channel.title: RC Car King
channel.description: Small cars. Big energy. The latest RC car reviews.

item.title: ARRMA Big Rock 223S DSC 4X4 review: a longer brushless crew-cab project
item.description: A longer crew-cab 4WD truck with a current center differential and 2S/3S DSC equipment. Its finished package suits sweeping outdoor routes, while separate power equipment and physical size remain real purchase decisions.

item.title: ARRMA Gorgon MEGA 550 review: a useful remaining-stock first monster package
item.description: A brushed rear-drive monster package with NiMH battery, USB charger and transmitter cells. The red SKU remains API-verifiable despite a manufacturer discontinued label, so compare the exact remaining-stock package and charging input needs.

item.title: ARRMA Granite 223S DSC 4X4 review: a deliberate entry into compact brushless bashing
item.description: A compact 4WD brushless monster with DSC and a current center differential. Its 2S/3S scope gives useful room to grow, while separate power equipment and conflicting tray lengths need attention.

item.title: ARRMA Kraton 6S BLX V6 review: a deliberate large-truck project for an experienced owner
item.description: A substantial 4S/6S RTR with current EXB-derived hardware, clipless body and separate receiver. It suits an experienced outdoor basher, provided space, compatible power equipment and the exact V6 specification are settled.

item.title: ARRMA Mojave 4S BLX review: a purposeful larger desert-truck package
item.description: A larger scale desert-truck RTR with a cockpit, inner body and three-differential 4WD. Its 3S/4S package suits an owner who wants the complete desert format, while power equipment, space and detailed-body upkeep add to ownership.

item.title: ARRMA Senton 223S DSC 4X4 review: a finished brushless short-course activity
item.description: A finished 4WD brushless short-course truck with DSC and 2S/3S scope. The enclosed body and current center differential suit a dirt-circuit project, while battery, charger and routine cleaning remain part of ownership.

item.title: ARRMA Typhon 223S DSC 4X4 review: a recreational buggy with a deliberate power plan
item.description: A complete 4WD brushless buggy with DSC and 2S/3S capability. It offers a clear recreational route, provided battery fit is verified and the 223S is distinguished from GROM, 6S and competition-oriented variants.

item.title: ARRMA Vorteks 223S DSC 4X4 review: a coordinated brushless stadium learning route
item.description: A finished brushless 4WD stadium truck with 2S/3S capability, DSC and a center differential. It offers a practical learning route, provided you budget power equipment and distinguish the separate 2WD version.

item.title: Axial SCX10 III Coyote review: the simplified body suits a driver who wants to use the obstacles?
item.description: A full-size SCX10 III purchase with a finished Coyote body, straight-axle layout and fitted radio. Drive battery and charger are extra; we assess the complete trail-ready shopping basket.

item.title: Axial SCX24 Chevrolet C10 1967–1972 review: choose the c10 for the years and details you can change?
item.description: A classic Chevrolet pickup in a small, battery-equipped crawler package. This review covers the newer AXI-3408 version, its ownership requirements and the manufacturer’s conflicting motor information.

item.title: Axial SCX24 Jeep JT Gladiator V2 review: the long pickup is the buying case?
item.description: A battery-equipped miniature Jeep with the Gladiator’s longer wheelbase and updated V2 package. Course size, body clearance and exact-generation equipment matter more than the scale badge alone.

item.title: Axial SCX24 Toyota 4Runner review: toyota detail makes this more than the cheapest entry route?
item.description: A miniature Toyota crawler with a finished 4Runner body and included power equipment. We unpack the package, useful indoor terrain and the conflicting published motor descriptions before making the buying call.

item.title: Axial SCX30 Ford Bronco review: a desktop bronco gives you a different reason to go smaller?
item.description: An especially small Bronco crawler with supplied battery equipment and a finished scale body. Its strongest buying case is a compact obstacle course, with terrain chosen for its actual dimensions.

item.title: Axial SCX30 Jeep Wrangler JLU review: the jeep is a small-course purchase with specific scale appeal?
item.description: A tiny Wrangler crawler with included power equipment and a detailed finished body. We focus on indoor-course fit, controls, the stock hardware and the limits of the published specification table.

item.title: Kyosho Fazer D2 Toyota 86 GT Tuned Lightning Red review: the right complete-car project?
item.description: A finished GT86 and coordinated steering/throttle assistance make a clear first RWD drift package; venue tires and separate power gear still need planning.

item.title: Kyosho Fazer Mk2 1971 Datsun 240Z Rally review: the right complete-car project?
item.description: A finished 240Z rally package with oil damping and chassis cover; choose manageable dirt and preserve the distinction from an ordinary touring Fazer.

item.title: Kyosho Fazer Mk2 1970 Dodge Charger Supercharged VE Gray review: the right complete-car project?
item.description: A complete brushless pavement car with the supercharged Charger finished; moving headlights, lighting and power equipment are separate decisions.

item.title: Kyosho Fazer Mk2 1969 Chevy El Camino SS396 Cortez Silver review: the right complete-car project?
item.description: A finished vintage pickup for smooth-ground driving; the long road chassis and discontinued manufacturer status require an informed purchase.

item.title: Kyosho Fazer Mk2 Nissan Skyline 2000GT-R KPGC10 Silver review: the right complete-car project?
item.description: The silver Hakosuka Readyset combines its exact scale subject with conventional fitted road hardware; keep the C revision and low-ground brief visible.

item.title: Kyosho Fazer Mk2 1970 Toyota Celica GT Orion Turquoise review: the right complete-car project?
item.description: A distinctive finished vintage Toyota for low-chassis pavement driving; power gear and optional illumination belong in the complete budget.

item.title: Kyosho KC10 Toyota Land Cruiser 60 Body Type1 review: the right complete-car project?
item.description: The early LC60 Readyset has a coherent scale-trail package and real straight axles; optional dig/two-speed features must stay separate from stock contents.

item.title: Kyosho Mini-Z 4x4 Toyota Land Cruiser 300 Precious White Pearl review: the right complete-car project?
item.description: A complete palm-sized LC300 for deliberate indoor crawling; eight AAA cells and a miniature course matter more than full-size trail expectations.

item.title: Losi Micro-B review: a real buggy for a very small race space?
item.description: A miniature rear-drive race buggy with an aluminum chassis, oil shocks and included battery equipment. The buying question is whether your indoor space gives this small car a useful circuit.

item.title: Losi Micro-T review: a short truck makes a different kind of indoor course?
item.description: A tiny stadium truck with a finished body, oil shocks and supplied battery equipment. Its compact size is appealing for indoor laps; surface choice and realistic obstacle scale still matter.

item.title: Losi Mini-B Brushless review: a miniature race buggy still needs a real place to run?
item.description: A brushless rear-drive buggy with its drive pack and charger included. Budget for the required USB input adapter, then check whether your local small-car circuit suits the tires and class.

item.title: Losi Mini LMT Grave Digger review: grave digger is the attraction, and solid axles are the reason to stay?
item.description: A compact Grave Digger monster truck with solid axles, four-wheel drive and supplied battery equipment. Buy it for that distinctive format; choose a suitable driving area before planning jumps or upgrades.

item.title: Losi Mini-T 2.0 Brushless review: the stadium-truck class should decide the purchase?
item.description: The newer Spektrum-powered Mini-T combines an assembled stadium truck with included battery equipment. The USB input adapter is extra, and this review keeps it distinct from older Dynamite-powered versions.

item.title: Redcat Danchee Ridgerock review: a budget crawler with four-wheel steering
item.description: An assembled 1/10 crawler with dual brushed motors, selectable four-wheel steering and included battery equipment. Here is the first-buyer case, the setup work and the upgrade tradeoff.

item.title: Tamiya BBX BB-01 review: the right complete-car project?
item.description: A detailed modern scale-buggy kit with worthwhile mechanical substance; the motor shaft and low-profile servo requirements are real purchase constraints.

item.title: Tamiya Fighter NXGEN DT-04 review: the right complete-car project?
item.description: A credible first contemporary buggy kit with oil dampers and a molded-panel body; verify the club rules and standard-size servo fit.

item.title: Tamiya The Frog (2005) review: the right complete-car project?
item.description: An unusually interesting classic build for the returning modeler; budget the electronics before enjoying its space-frame and suspension detail.

item.title: Tamiya The Grasshopper II (2017) review: the right complete-car project?
item.description: A simple molded-body classic for a first kit build; choose it for the stock 380-powered project before budgeting extensive conversions.

item.title: Tamiya The Hornet review: the right complete-car project?
item.description: The original Hornet build remains compelling for its own identity; oil-damped rear axle and supplied 540 are useful, but it is a classic project.

item.title: Tamiya Midnight Pumpkin Metallic Special review: the right complete-car project?
item.description: A plated custom-pickup build for relaxed wheelie-oriented fun; its tall stance and simple suspension deserve realistic expectations.

item.title: Tamiya Subaru Impreza Monte-Carlo ’99 TT-02 review: the right complete-car project?
item.description: A blue-and-gold body project with a clear mild-rally role; friction damping and discontinued regional stock deserve attention alongside the livery.

item.title: Tamiya Toyota Celica GT-Four ST165 TT-02 review: the right complete-car project?
item.description: An appealing ST165 model for smooth-ground driving; confirm the regional body finish and ESC before treating the low kit offer as a finished basket.

item.title: Team Associated DC10 Drift RTR review: the dc10 is a first dedicated drift car with room to learn setup?
item.description: An assembled RWD drifter with a G10 chassis, brushless motor and adjustable gyro. The standard blue RTR still needs power equipment; we explain the setup decisions before the first slide.

item.title: Team Associated Pro2 SC10 Method Race Wheels review: the pro2 is for a driver who actually wants rear-drive short course?
item.description: A rear-drive short-course truck with a finished Method Race Wheels body and DVC control equipment. The standard RTR needs its own power equipment; we assess terrain, setup and the total purchase.

item.title: Team Associated Reflex 14R Hoonicorn review: buy the hoonicorn for pavement play and the licensed car?
item.description: A compact four-wheel-drive Hoonicorn with a finished licensed body and brushed power. Battery and charger are extra, and the full-size car’s headline horsepower has nothing to do with this RC package.

item.title: Team Associated Rival MT10 V2 review: the mt10 is the outdoor monster-truck route?
item.description: A four-wheel-drive brushless monster truck in the red V2 standard package. The battery and charger are extra; we separate this purchase from brushed, Combo and Factory Team versions.

item.title: Team Associated SR10M Dirt Oval LiPo Combo review: an oval venue makes this car make sense?
item.description: A dirt-oval car bundled with a Reedy LiPo and balance charger. This review covers the 70033C Combo, explains what it adds to the standard RTR and checks the track-fit buying case.

item.title: Traxxas 4-Tec Drift Nissan 240SX review: a proper first step sideways?
item.description: A complete RWD drift car with an S13 shell, adjustable driving assistance and two tire compounds. Here’s what you’re buying, what you still need, and where the compromises show up.

item.title: Traxxas Bandit 2WD XL-5 review: a credible first buggy for a prepared route
item.description: A complete brushed buggy with battery and charger for firm-ground practice. It offers a clear first project, provided your terrain fits the narrow format and upgrades can wait.

item.title: Traxxas Maxx review: a substantial step-up monster package
item.description: A substantial WideMaxx brushless monster truck for a deliberate step up. Its 3S/4S capability and factory suspension need suitable space, storage and a complete LiPo charging budget.

item.title: Traxxas Rustler 2WD XL-5 review: a useful stock stadium-truck starting point
item.description: A finished brushed stadium truck with a NiMH pack and USB-C charger. Exposed wheels and simple controls suit a first circuit; thick lawn and immediate brushless plans complicate value.

item.title: Traxxas Rustler 4X4 Ultimate review: factory equipment for a real upgrade plan
item.description: A brushless 4WD stadium truck with factory GTR shocks, sway bars and connected radio equipment. The upgrades earn value when you wanted them already; battery and charger remain extra.

item.title: Traxxas Slash 2WD XL-5 review: a coherent first short-course package
item.description: A battery-inclusive brushed short-course truck for learning rear-drive lines. Its practical package is appealing, but grass, charging input power and future conversion spending need checking.

item.title: Traxxas Stampede 2WD XL-5 review: a purposeful first tall rear-drive truck
item.description: A tall rear-drive monster truck with supplied NiMH charging equipment. Clearance has a clear purpose, while traction, cornering inputs and the missing USB power supply still matter.

item.title: Traxxas TRX-4 Sport review: simple functions, serious trail hardware
item.description: A full-size RTR crawler with portals, permanent locks and one gear. The simpler operating brief is persuasive for slow trail learning, but battery and charger add to the startup basket.

item.title: Traxxas TRX-4M Ford Bronco review: a complete small bronco crawling project
item.description: A licensed small Bronco crawler with a dedicated LiPo and USB charger. Nearby obstacles suit its size; stock bushings, integrated electronics and upgrade spending deserve an honest look.
